subject: Hosted API — Customer purge & custody playbook (Q&A)
messages:
From: Tara Singh <security@glimmer.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>
Cc: Liam O'Neill <dpo@glimmer.ai>
Date: Thu, 01 Jul 2027 16:23:00 -0700
Subject: Security questionnaire - data purge & custody details

Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week. As part of our procurement security review, we need a short Q&A on how Redwood handles customer-initiated data purge requests and custody of ephemeral data in the Hosted API. Our legal team wants clear steps we can include in our contract appendix. High level questions below — please keep answers brief and process-oriented.

1) When a customer requests a full data purge for their tenant, what is the end-to-end timeline and what systems are touched?
2) Do you retain any backups, snapshots, or logs containing customer inputs beyond the purge window? If so, what is retention and how is deletion confirmed?
3) How does the hosted runtime treat ephemeral (inference) state and KV caches? Are any artifacts persisted to durable storage?
4) Are there circumstances (e.g., legal hold, billing dispute) where you will not perform a purge? If so, escalation path?
5) Can you provide a one-page playbook we can attach to the contract describing the purge flow and verification?

Thanks,
Tara
Tara Singh
Head of Security
Glimmer.ai

From: Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 09:12:33 -0700
Subject: Re: Fwd: Security questionnaire - data purge & custody details

Karthik / Marissa — draft below (technical). I tried to be succinct for a contract appendix. Feel free to shorten.

1) End-to-end timeline and systems touched:
- A standard tenant purge (customer-initiated via Console API/Support) triggers: (a) immediate removal from primary object stores (S3/Blob) where customer request logs and long-term inputs are stored; (b) queued deletion across indexing systems (Elasticsearch), metrics pipelines, and internal analytics; (c) invalidation of tenant keys in cache layers and eviction of KV caches across serving nodes.
- Typical timeline: automated purge completes within 72 hours for account metadata and stored requests; propagation to analytics/indices completes within 7 calendar days.

2) Backups, snapshots, logs:
- Operational backups are taken for disaster recovery with a maximum retention of 30 days for account-level snapshots. Backups are encrypted and stored in a segregated recovery bucket labeled "recovery/short-term".
- On a customer-initiated purge we perform a targeted removal from active backups within the 30-day window where feasible and mark the account as purged so restores exclude that tenant. Complete physical removal from immutable backups (if they exist due to retention windows) is performed as part of the next regular backup rotation; we provide attestations of deletion and timestamps.

3) Ephemeral inference state and KV caches:
- Inference requests are processed in-memory; KV caches used for acceleration are persisted only to in-memory stores or local ephemeral NVMe on serving hosts. No permanent storage of raw prompts or model outputs is written to durable customer-visible object store by default.
- Telemetry/metrics emitted are aggregated and anonymized; raw request payloads are not retained in metrics streams beyond diagnostic windows (14 days).

4) Exceptions and escalation:
- We will delay or refuse purge only under narrow conditions: active legal hold with court order, ongoing fraud/billing investigation tied to the account, or explicit regulatory obligations.
- Escalation: Support -> Security (Irene) -> Legal (Marissa) -> Customer (formal response). Provide a ticket reference and expected timeline for resolution.

5) Playbook
- I'll attach a one-page playbook. It contains the API call, expected timeline, verification steps, and contact points for exceptions.

Notes: I recommend including the 72-hour/7-day timelines and the 30-day backup window in the contract appendix.

Irene Choi
Senior Security Engineer, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
To: Tara Singh <security@glimmer.ai>, Liam O'Neill <dpo@glimmer.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.ai>, Irene Choi <irene@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 02 Jul 2027 14:08:55 -0700
Subject: Re: Security questionnaire - data purge & custody details

Hi Tara / Liam — thanks for the clear list. Below are Redwood's contract-ready answers and the attached one-page playbook. We've kept the language actionable and suitable for an appendix.

Answers (to include in appendix):
1) Purge timeline & systems: "Customer-initiated tenant purge via the Console or API triggers automated removal from primary stores within 72 hours. Index and analytics propagation completes within 7 calendar days. Systems affected include object storage, search indices, metrics pipelines, and cache invalidation across serving nodes."

2) Backups & confirmation: "Redwood retains short-term disaster recovery snapshots for up to 30 days. Following a purge request we exclude the tenant from subsequent restores and perform targeted deletion from active backups where feasible. Redwood provides a signed attestation with timestamps confirming completion of the purge."

3) Ephemeral inference & caches: "Inference inputs are processed in-memory and cached only on ephemeral host storage or in-memory caches. Redwood does not persist raw prompts or generated outputs to durable customer-facing object stores by default. Aggregated telemetry is retained for 14 days for diagnostics and anonymized reporting."

4) Exceptions: "Purges may be delayed or withheld only for lawful reasons (court order/legal hold), ongoing fraud/billing investigations, or explicit regulatory requirements. In such cases, Redwood will notify the customer, provide the legal basis, and route the matter through an agreed escalation path."

5) Playbook: Attached: redwood_custody_playbook_v1.2.pdf (one page)

If this looks good, we can add the same text into the contract appendix and sign off.

Best,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Compliance (on behalf of Legal), Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_custody_playbook_v1.2.pdf (one-page playbook), residency_matrix_snapshot.xlsx

Tara / Liam — quick follow-up to confirm both asks.

1) Backup removals: We will target physical removal of snapshots containing tenant metadata within the 30-day operational backup window wherever engineering and cloud provider policies allow. In practice this means: (a) for short-term recovery snapshots under our control we perform object-level deletion so restores will not return purged data; (b) for immutable provider-managed snapshots that cannot be modified mid-cycle, we mark the tenant as purged and ensure the snapshot is omitted from any restore operations; those snapshots are destroyed on the provider's normal rotation schedule (<= 30 days). We will document any provider-imposed constraints in the attestation.

2) Attestation format: Redwood will provide a signed PDF attestation with: customer tenant id, request timestamp, purge completion timestamp(s), systems affected, and a redwood legal signature block. We can deliver the attestation via DocuSign or as a signed PDF, per your preference.

If you'd like, we can add a short clause in the appendix that describes the provider-managed snapshot behavior verbatim.

Regards,
Marissa Cole
Head of Product Compliance, Redwood Inference

Attachments included in thread: redwood_custody_playbook_v1.2.pdf, residency_matrix_snapshot.xlsx
